title: A Water Bill People Can Interpret
transcript:
A town's water department has redesigned its household bills after finding that many residents could not explain why their payments had changed. The old bill displayed a total charge and a meter reading, but it did little to distinguish changes in consumption from changes in the length of the billing period.

During interviews, some residents said that a higher bill necessarily meant they had become less careful. Yet a bill covering more days could increase even when average daily use remained stable. The department's customer-service team spent considerable time explaining this point to callers, suggesting that the document itself was not doing an adequate job.

The new design shows average daily consumption beside the total amount used. It also compares the household with its own use during the same season of the previous year. Officials rejected an early proposal to rank every household against a town-wide average. Household size and other circumstances vary, and the comparison could have encouraged unfair conclusions about individual behaviour.

In the first trial, residents receiving the revised bill answered questions about their usage more accurately. Calls about unexpected charges declined. However, the department did not claim that the new design had reduced water consumption. That would require observations over a longer period and an allowance for weather conditions that affect outdoor use.

The project leader describes the bill as a tool for understanding before it becomes a tool for changing habits. People who can distinguish a longer billing period from a genuine rise in daily demand are better placed to investigate a problem. The next version will include a clearer explanation of estimated readings, following feedback from residents whose meters could not always be accessed.

questions.prompt: Why could a household receive a higher bill without increasing its average daily water use?
options: The town had stopped recording meter readings.
The bill could cover a greater number of days.
Every bill included the same estimate regardless of use.
The household had automatically been charged for its neighbours.
questions.answer: The bill could cover a greater number of days.
questions.explanation: 账期天数更长会增加总费用，即使日均用水没有上升。

questions.prompt: What comparison does the redesigned bill provide?
options: The household’s use in the same season of the previous year.
The names of the town’s highest-consuming households.
The water prices in every neighbouring country.
The daily use of the department’s office staff.
questions.answer: The household’s use in the same season of the previous year.
questions.explanation: 新版与该户上一年相同季节的用水情况比较，而非简单排名。

questions.prompt: Why was a town-wide household ranking rejected?
options: No household had ever supplied a meter reading.
The department wanted to remove all comparisons.
Differences in household circumstances could make it misleading.
Residents were already receiving individual rankings every week.
questions.answer: Differences in household circumstances could make it misleading.
questions.explanation: 家庭人数和具体情况不同，统一排名可能导致不公平或误导性的行为评价。

questions.prompt: What did the first trial establish?
options: The new bill eliminated the need for meter readings.
Town-wide water demand had permanently declined.
Weather no longer affected household use.
Residents understood their usage more accurately.
questions.answer: Residents understood their usage more accurately.
questions.explanation: 试验显示理解准确度提高和疑问电话减少，尚不能证明用水量下降。
